purpose: Probenecid is used to treat gout and high uric acid levels in your blood. It helps prevent painful gout attacks by keeping uric acid from building up in your joints. It can also be used alongside certain antibiotics to help them work better and last longer in your body.
how_it_works: Your kidneys normally filter uric acid, but sometimes they hold onto too much of it, which causes it to build up and form sharp crystals in your joints — that is what causes gout pain. Probenecid works by telling your kidneys to release more uric acid into your urine so it gets flushed out of your body. Think of it like opening a drain to let the extra uric acid wash away.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, or loss of appetite are the most common. You might also notice headache, dizziness, flushing, or more frequent urination. Some people develop a mild skin rash.
warnings: Drink plenty of water every day — at least 6 to 8 glasses — to prevent kidney stones while taking this medicine. Do not take aspirin while using probenecid because aspirin can block how well it works. This medication is not used during an active gout flare-up — it can actually make things worse at first. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or a peptic ulcer before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 250 mg (one tablet) twice a day for the first week. After that, your doctor will likely increase it to 500 mg twice a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose depending on your uric acid levels. Always take it with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.
